root_cause: The ArrowRight key handler in tab.js activates the next tab but does not move focus to it after blurring the previously active tab, leaving focus on the page body.
repair_strategy: Add a focus() call on the newly activated tab element immediately after invoking its show() method in the _keydown handler.
expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing ArrowRight (or ArrowLeft) will move focus to the adjacent tab, update its aria-selected to true, and keep focus within the tablist.
functional_risks: Potential duplicate focus if the show() method later changes to include focus handling.
If the tab is not visually visible due to a fade transition, focus may land on a non‑visible element, though it remains programmatically focusable.
verification_requirements: After ArrowRight from the active tab, focus must be on the next tab and its aria-selected must be true.
After ArrowLeft from the active tab, focus must be on the previous tab and its aria-selected must be true.
Tab panel visibility must update correctly when focus changes via arrow keys.
Ensure that initial tab navigation with Tab key still works as specified in regression guards.
